title: Classification of Matter
seo_title: SSS 1 Chemistry: Classification of Matter Worksheets (WAEC/NECO)
standard_text: Matter is classified as mixtures (homogeneous and heterogeneous) or pure substances (elements and compounds); materials are described by their properties: metals, non-metals and metalloids, electrical and thermal conductors and insulators, and magnetic and non-magnetic materials. Names and formulae of substances. (summary of the senior secondary Chemistry curriculum, SSS 1; WAEC and NECO syllabuses)
meta_desc: Free SSS 1 Chemistry worksheets (senior secondary curriculum, WAEC and NECO): mixtures and pure substances, elements and compounds, metals, non-metals and metalloids, names and formulae and separating mixtures. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Matter is a mixture or a pure substance.
key_sub: Pure substances are elements or compounds.
body_html:
How to think about it

A mixture has two or more substances that are not chemically joined; it can be separated by physical methods. A homogeneous mixture (such as salt water) is the same throughout; a heterogeneous mixture (such as sand in water) is not.

A pure substance has a fixed composition. An element has only one kind of atom; a compound has two or more elements chemically bonded in a fixed ratio, such as H₂O. Metals are shiny, malleable and conduct heat and electricity; metalloids such as silicon have properties of both metals and non-metals.

Example

Is air an element, a compound or a mixture?

Its gases are not bonded together.

Answer: a homogeneous mixture

Example

Is carbon dioxide an element or a compound?

CO₂ has two kinds of atom bonded together.

Answer: a compound

Common mistakes

  • Thinking a compound is the same as a mixture.
  • Thinking all metals are magnetic (only iron, cobalt and nickel are).
  • Thinking a solution is a pure substance.

faq.q: How can you separate a mixture?
faq.a: By physical methods such as filtration, evaporation, distillation and chromatography.
An element, such as silicon or germanium, with properties of both metals and non-metals.

items.q: Is sulfuric acid (H<sub>2</sub>SO<sub>4</sub>) a molecule of an element or of a compound?
items.e: It contains atoms of more than one element chemically combined.

items.q: Chiamaka built this model. Each ball is an atom (H = hydrogen, O = oxygen, C = carbon, N = nitrogen). Which formula matches it?
items.e: Count each kind of atom: 2 nitrogen.

items.q: Tobi sorts substances. Which one is a compound (two or more kinds of atoms bonded together)?
items.e: A compound contains two or more different elements chemically joined.

items.q: Is oxygen gas (O<sub>2</sub>) a molecule of an element or of a compound?
items.e: It contains only one type of atom.

items.q: Is flour stirred into water a solution or a suspension?
items.e: A solution is clear and does not settle; a suspension is cloudy, its solid particles settle and can be filtered.

items.q: Hadiza sorts substances. Which one is an element (made of only one kind of atom)?
items.e: An element contains only one kind of atom, even if the atoms are joined in pairs.

items.q: Is chalk powder shaken in water a solution or a suspension?
items.e: A solution is clear and does not settle; a suspension is cloudy, its solid particles settle and can be filtered.

items.q: Is sugar dissolved in water a solution or a suspension?
items.e: The solute is dissolved, so the liquid is clear and nothing settles.

items.q: Is salt water a solution or a suspension?
items.e: The solute is dissolved, so the liquid is clear and nothing settles.

items.q: Tolu sorts substances. Which one is an element (made of only one kind of atom)?
items.e: An element contains only one kind of atom, even if the atoms are joined in pairs.

items.q: Babatunde built this model. Each ball is an atom (H = hydrogen, O = oxygen, C = carbon, N = nitrogen). Which formula matches it?

items.e: A compound contains two or more different elements chemically joined.

items.q: Obinna built this model. Each ball is an atom (H = hydrogen, O = oxygen, C = carbon, N = nitrogen). Which formula matches it?

items.q: The formula of ammonia is NH<sub>3</sub>. How many atoms are in one molecule?
items.e: Add the numbers: 1 + 3 = 4.

items.q: Femi built this model. Each ball is an atom (H = hydrogen, O = oxygen, C = carbon, N = nitrogen). Which formula matches it?
items.e: Count each kind of atom: 1 carbon, 2 oxygen.

items.q: Is copper(II) sulfate dissolved in water a solution or a suspension?
items.e: The solute is dissolved, so the liquid is clear and nothing settles.

items.q: Dayo sorts substances. Which one is a compound (two or more kinds of atoms bonded together)?
items.e: A compound contains two or more different elements chemically joined.

items.q: The formula of methane is CH<sub>4</sub>. How many different types of atoms are in one molecule?
items.e: Count the different symbols: carbon, hydrogen.

items.q: Dayo measures an unknown substance. Its density is 5.24 g/cm³. Using a reference table, which substance could it be?
items.e: Density is a characteristic property: rust (iron oxide) has a density of 5.24 g/cm³.

items.q: What is the formula of magnesium nitride?
items.e: Mg<sup>2+</sup> and N<sup>3−</sup>: the charges must balance, so the formula is Mg<sub>3</sub>N<sub>2</sub>.

items.q: Victor observes that a glass bottle breaks. Is this a chemical change or a physical change?
c: a chemical change, because it looks different
a chemical change, because a new substance forms
a physical change, because no new substance forms
items.e: The substance is still the same; only its shape, size or state changed.

items.q: A material changes from liquid to gas at 78 °C. Which physical property is being described?
items.e: This is the boiling point of the material.

items.q: Nkechi lists changes in the kitchen. Which is a chemical change?
c: a glow stick is bent and starts to glow
items.e: A new substance with new properties forms.

items.q: Tobi lists changes around the house. Which is a physical change?
c: clay is shaped into a bowl
two clear liquids mix and form a solid yellow powder
a glow stick is bent and starts to glow
items.e: The substance stays the same.

items.q: What is the name of MgCl<sub>2</sub>?
items.e: Name the metal, then the non-metal with -ide. Ionic names do not use prefixes.

items.q: A material can hold a heavy load without breaking. Which physical property is being described?
items.e: This is the strength of the material.

items.q: What is the name of Ca<sub>3</sub>N<sub>2</sub>?
items.e: Name the metal, then the non-metal with -ide. Ionic names do not use prefixes.

items.q: What is the name of Li<sub>3</sub>N?
items.e: Name the metal, then the non-metal with -ide. Ionic names do not use prefixes.

items.q: What is the formula of aluminium sulfide?
items.e: Al<sup>3+</sup> and S<sup>2−</sup>: the charges must balance, so the formula is Al<sub>2</sub>S<sub>3</sub>.

items.q: A material has a mass of 7.9 g for every 1 cm³. Which physical property is being described?
items.e: This is the density of the material.

items.q: What is the name of MgS?
items.e: Name the metal, then the non-metal with -ide. Ionic names do not use prefixes.

items.q: Chidi observes that two clear liquids mix and form a solid yellow powder. Is this a chemical change or a physical change?
c: a physical change, because it is a mixture
a physical change, because only the shape or state changes
a chemical change, because a new substance forms
items.e: Gas, colour change, new smell, light, heat or a new solid are signs of a new substance.

items.q: What is the formula of magnesium sulfide?
items.e: Mg<sup>2+</sup> and S<sup>2−</sup>: the charges must balance, so the formula is MgS.

items.q: Kemi observes that a copper statue turns green over many years. Is this a chemical change or a physical change?
c: a chemical change, because a new substance forms
a physical change, because it is a mixture
a physical change, because only the shape or state changes
items.e: Gas, colour change, new smell, light, heat or a new solid are signs of a new substance.

items.q: What is the formula of calcium oxide?
items.e: Ca<sup>2+</sup> and O<sup>2−</sup>: the charges must balance, so the formula is CaO.

items.q: What is the name of Na<sub>2</sub>S?
items.e: Name the metal, then the non-metal with -ide. Ionic names do not use prefixes.

items.q: Ife lists changes around the house. Which is a physical change?
c: a glow stick is bent and starts to glow
a copper statue turns green over many years
items.e: The substance stays the same.

items.q: Gbenga lists changes in the kitchen. Which is a chemical change?
c: food is digested in the stomach
a piece of paper is cut into strips
items.e: A new substance with new properties forms.

items.q: Which element has chemical properties most like bromine (Br)?
items.e: Same group = same number of valence electrons.

items.q: Which is more reactive, fluorine (F) or chlorine (Cl)?
items.e: Halogens get less reactive down the group (harder to gain 1 electron).

items.q: A polymer chain is made of 5,000 units of ethene (C₂H₄, 28 g/mol). About what is its molar mass?
What kind of structure does iodine have?
items.e: Weak van der Waals forces between I₂ molecules, so it sublimes easily.

items.q: Many glucose monomers are linked in a long chain. Which polymer forms?
items.e: Polymers are chains of repeating monomers.

items.q: Which is more reactive: iodine or chlorine?
items.e: Reactivity of the halogens decreases down Group 17.

items.q: Which element is one of the alkaline earth metals?
items.e: Calcium is in group 2.

items.q: Which element has chemical properties most like argon (Ar)?
items.e: Same group = same number of valence electrons.

items.q: Which element has chemical properties most like neon (Ne)?
items.e: Same group = same number of valence electrons.

items.q: Which is more reactive with water: sodium or potassium?
items.e: Reactivity of Group 1 metals increases down the group: the outer electron is further from the nucleus and lost more easily.

items.q: What type of bonding is in sodium chloride?
items.e: Electrostatic attraction between oppositely charged ions.

items.q: Which is more reactive, chlorine (Cl) or bromine (Br)?
items.e: Halogens get less reactive down the group (harder to gain 1 electron).

items.q: Why do the boiling points of the noble gases increase down the group?
c: there are more electrons, so van der Waals forces are stronger
items.e: Bigger atoms have bigger induced dipole–dipole forces.

items.q: Which substance conducts electricity when molten but not when solid?
items.e: Ions are fixed in the solid but free to move when molten.

items.q: Which is more reactive, fluorine (F) or iodine (I)?
items.e: Halogens get less reactive down the group (harder to gain 1 electron).

items.q: Which type of bonding is found in sodium chloride?
items.e: A metal and a non-metal: electron transfer.

items.q: Which is more reactive, sodium (Na) or potassium (K)?
items.e: Alkali metals get more reactive down the group (easier to lose 1 electron).

items.q: Why are metals malleable?
c: layers of cations can slide over each other while the delocalised electrons keep holding them together
the ions repel each other strongly
items.e: Metallic bonding is not directional.

items.q: Many amino acids monomers are linked in a long chain. Which polymer forms?
items.e: Polymers are chains of repeating monomers.

items.q: What is the bond angle in PCl<sub>5</sub>?
items.e: 5 bonding pairs, 0 lone pairs. Lone pairs repel more than bonding pairs, so each lone pair closes the angle by about 2.5°.

items.q: Uche looks up methane, CH<sub>4</sub>. How many atoms are in one molecule?
items.e: 1 carbon + 4 hydrogen = 5 atoms.

items.q: Ikenna studies making salt: 2Na + Cl2 → 2NaCl. How many sodium atoms are in the reactants (left side)?
items.e: Multiply each coefficient by the subscript and add. The number is the same on both sides: 2.

items.q: Babatunde studies making ammonia: N2 + 3H2 → 2NH3. How many nitrogen atoms are in the reactants (left side)?
items.e: Multiply each coefficient by the subscript and add. The number is the same on both sides: 2.

items.q: Na<sup>+</sup> and O<sup>2−</sup> ions combine. What is the formula of the compound?
items.e: Use the lowest numbers that make the total charge zero: 2 × (+1) + 1 × (−2) = 0.

items.q: Esther writes 2H<sub>2</sub>O<sub>2</sub>. How many hydrogen atoms are there in all?
items.e: The coefficient 2 multiplies everything: 2 × 2 = 4.

items.q: Ada looks up hydrogen peroxide, H<sub>2</sub>O<sub>2</sub>. How many atoms are in one molecule?
items.e: 2 hydrogen + 2 oxygen = 4 atoms.

items.q: How many oxygen atoms are in one molecule of hydrogen peroxide, H<sub>2</sub>O<sub>2</sub>?
items.e: The subscript after O is 2.

items.q: Zainab writes 2CaCO<sub>3</sub>. How many carbon atoms are there in all?
items.e: The coefficient 2 multiplies everything: 2 × 1 = 2.

items.q: Samuel looks up sulfuric acid, H<sub>2</sub>SO<sub>4</sub>. How many atoms are in one molecule?
items.e: 2 hydrogen + 1 sulfur + 4 oxygen = 7 atoms.

items.q: Bisi writes 4CaCO<sub>3</sub>. How many calcium atoms are there in all?
items.e: The coefficient 4 multiplies everything: 4 × 1 = 4.

items.q: Abdullahi looks up glucose (sugar), C<sub>6</sub>H<sub>12</sub>O<sub>6</sub>. How many atoms are in one molecule?
items.e: 6 carbon + 12 hydrogen + 6 oxygen = 24 atoms.

items.q: Nonso writes 2CaCO<sub>3</sub>. How many calcium atoms are there in all?
items.e: The coefficient 2 multiplies everything: 2 × 1 = 2.

items.q: What is the formula of strontium chloride?
items.e: Strontium forms Sr<sup>2+</sup> and chlorine forms Cl<sup>−</sup>; the charges must add to zero.

items.q: Obinna writes 4NH<sub>3</sub>. How many hydrogen atoms are there in all?
items.e: The coefficient 4 multiplies everything: 4 × 3 = 12.

items.q: Li<sup>+</sup> and P<sup>3−</sup> ions combine. What is the formula of the compound?
items.e: Use the lowest numbers that make the total charge zero: 3 × (+1) + 1 × (−3) = 0.

items.q: Nonso studies magnesium burning: 2Mg + O2 → 2MgO. How many magnesium atoms are in the reactants (left side)?
items.e: Multiply each coefficient by the subscript and add. The number is the same on both sides: 2.

items.q: Nkechi writes 3CH<sub>4</sub>. How many hydrogen atoms are there in all?
items.e: The coefficient 3 multiplies everything: 3 × 4 = 12.

items.q: Hadiza writes 3C<sub>3</sub>H<sub>8</sub>. How many hydrogen atoms are there in all?
items.e: The coefficient 3 multiplies everything: 3 × 8 = 24.

items.q: Fatima writes 2H<sub>2</sub>O. How many oxygen atoms are there in all?
items.e: The coefficient 2 multiplies everything: 2 × 1 = 2.

items.q: Chidi looks up carbon dioxide, CO<sub>2</sub>. How many atoms are in one molecule?
items.e: 1 carbon + 2 oxygen = 3 atoms.

items.q: How can sand be separated from salt water?
items.e: Insoluble solids stay on the filter paper.

items.q: In a bond between strontium (Sr) and fluorine (F) (electronegativities 0.95 and 3.98), which atom gets a partial negative charge?
c: Neither; the electrons are shared equally.
items.e: The more electronegative atom pulls the shared electrons closer.

items.q: Electronegativity: phosphorus (P) = 2.19 and chlorine (Cl) = 3.16. What type of bond forms between them?
items.e: Difference = 0.97. Below 0.4: nonpolar; 0.4–1.7: polar covalent; above 1.7: ionic.

items.q: In thin-layer chromatography a spot moves 3.1 cm and the solvent front moves 6.5 cm. Calculate the R<sub>f</sub> value.
items.e: Rf = distance moved by spot ÷ distance moved by solvent = 0.477.

items.q: In thin-layer chromatography a spot moves 2.4 cm and the solvent front moves 10 cm. Calculate the R<sub>f</sub> value.
items.e: Rf = distance moved by spot ÷ distance moved by solvent = 0.240.

items.e: Rf = distance moved by spot ÷ distance moved by solvent = 0.150.

items.q: In thin-layer chromatography a spot moves 5.2 cm and the solvent front moves 6.5 cm. Calculate the R<sub>f</sub> value.
items.e: Rf = distance moved by spot ÷ distance moved by solvent = 0.800.

items.q: Why does graphite conduct electricity but diamond does not?
c: each carbon in graphite bonds to three others, leaving one delocalised electron
items.e: The electrons move along the layers.

items.q: Why do metals conduct electricity?
c: they have a sea of delocalised electrons that can move through the lattice
their ions move to the electrodes
items.e: Electrons carry the charge.

items.q: In thin-layer chromatography a spot moves 3.6 cm and the solvent front moves 7.0 cm. Calculate the R<sub>f</sub> value.
items.e: Rf = distance moved by spot ÷ distance moved by solvent = 0.514.

items.q: In thin-layer chromatography a spot moves 4.5 cm and the solvent front moves 9.0 cm. Calculate the R<sub>f</sub> value.
items.e: Rf = distance moved by spot ÷ distance moved by solvent = 0.500.

items.q: What is an alloy?
c: a mixture of a metal with other elements, such as steel (iron and carbon)
items.e: Different-sized atoms stop layers sliding, so alloys are harder.

items.e: Ethanol boils at 78 °C, water at 100 °C.
